critical_code_review_comments: brsf_excel.py _read_csv() splits rows with str.splitlines()+csv.reader but the CSV writer uses commas without quoting; if any employee full_name/team ever contains a comma the row will be misaligned. Add csv.reader over a StringIO of the raw text (already done) but the pytest here rebuilds the CSV with a naive ','.join which is only safe because no test names contain commas — production data should still be safe because openpyxl values are simple strings, but consider quoting on export for robustness.

brsf_excel.brsf_import_confirm() sets line['override_reason'] only for the override branch — manual entries do not record a distinct 'reason' field on the star line (only in the audit collection). If HR later views the manual dialog, they will see the imported value with no source hint. Consider stamping line['manual_reason'] = f"{source} — {filename}" for symmetry.

brsf_import_batches documents are never garbage-collected; a long-running system will accumulate one document per preview click even when the user cancels. Add a TTL index or a periodic cleanup job for batches with applied=false older than X days.

_read_xlsx() reads meta_month from the FIRST metadata row only (meta_month = meta_month or …). Since all rows share the same month this is fine, but if a file is manually re-saved with a modified metadata sheet the guard silently uses the first row. Consider asserting all rows share the same month.

BrsfExportImport.jsx download() uses `format` as the extension for both XLSX and CSV — 'xlsx' happens to be the correct extension but the code accepts arbitrary formats; harmless today, worth an allow-list.
Existing iteration_71 observations still apply: BrsfFramework.jsx is ~808 lines (recommend extracting dialog components) and StarReward.js still ships unreachable legacy dialogs — safe to prune.
